case_title: HMT Watches Ltd. v. M.A. Abida & Anr.
statutory_provisions: IPC s. 138; Negotiable Instruments Act s. 138
offence_finally_established: Section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act
neutral_facts: The appellant filed criminal complaint cases against the respondent, stating that 57 cheques dated 28.09.2006 were issued by the respondent in discharge of outstanding liability towards the appellant. When the cheques were presented for collection, they were dishonoured by bankers with the endorsement 'payment stopped by the drawer'. A notice of demand was issued by the appellant to the respondent, but the respondent failed to make the payment and instead disputed the liability. The respondent filed petitions challenging the criminal proceedings, arguing that the cheques were given as security and there was no outstanding liability. The High Court quashed the criminal complaints, but the Supreme Court held that the High Court exceeded its jurisdiction by quashing the proceedings and that the accused could be liable under Section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act even if the cheques were dishonoured due to a stop-payment instruction.
